PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.1 Information Security Policy
rationale: Req 12.1 requires an information security policy that is established, published, maintained, reviewed at least annually and disseminated to personnel. Security Policies defines the enforceable information-security expectations that policy document carries and governs its review cycle.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.2 Acceptable Use Policies
rationale: Req 12.2 requires acceptable use policies for end-user technologies. Security Policies sets the enforceable rules for how systems and devices in the cardholder data environment may be used.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.1.3 and 12.1.4 Roles, Responsibilities and Executive Accountability
rationale: Req 12.1.3 requires defined and acknowledged information security roles and responsibilities, and 12.1.4 assigns overall responsibility to an executive. Charters & Committees establishes the formal governance bodies and documented accountability that carry those assignments.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.3 Risk Management and Targeted Risk Analyses
rationale: Req 12.3.1 requires targeted risk analyses for each requirement that allows a frequency to be set, and 12.3.2 requires a TRA for each control implemented with the customized approach. The Cybersecurity Risk-Management Program provides the documented risk analysis method and approvals those TRAs depend on.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.5 PCI DSS Scope Documentation and Req 1.2.4 System Component Inventory
rationale: Req 12.5.1 requires an inventory of in-scope system components, 12.5.2 requires scope to be documented and confirmed at least annually, and 1.2.4 requires an accurate inventory of system components. System Asset Management maintains the authoritative, owned inventory of systems and data stores from which PCI scope is derived and validated.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.5.2 Scope Confirmation and Req 1.2.3 Network Diagrams
rationale: Req 12.5.2 requires the entity to document and confirm the accuracy of PCI DSS scope, and 1.2.3 requires diagrams of account data flows. Security Scope establishes which assets and environments the security program protects and how protection is proportionate to criticality, which is the scoping decision PCI DSS validates.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 1 Network Security Controls
rationale: Req 1 requires network security controls (firewalls and similar) to restrict traffic to and from the cardholder data environment, with a deny-all default and documented rule justification. Network Security designs and enforces segmentation and traffic control between trust zones.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 2 Secure Configurations
rationale: Req 2 requires secure configuration of all system components, including changing vendor defaults, hardening standards and removing unnecessary services. Platform Security hardens cloud, container and host platforms through controlled configuration baselines.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 2.2.1 Configuration Standards
rationale: Req 2.2.1 requires configuration standards that address known vulnerabilities and are consistent with industry hardening standards. Security Standards defines the enforceable technical hardening baselines that those configuration standards document.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 3 Protect Stored Account Data
rationale: Req 3 requires stored PAN to be rendered unreadable, with documented key management covering generation, distribution, storage, rotation and retirement. Cryptographic Management governs approved algorithms, key management and encryption of stored data.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 3.2 and 3.3 Account Data Storage and Retention and Req 3.4 PAN Masking
rationale: Req 3.2 limits storage of account data to what is needed with defined retention and secure deletion, 3.3 prohibits storing sensitive authentication data after authorization, and 3.4 requires PAN to be masked when displayed. Classification & Handling applies the sensitivity-based handling, retention and display rules to cardholder data.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 4 Protect Cardholder Data in Transit
rationale: Req 4 requires strong cryptography and secure protocols to protect PAN during transmission over open, public networks. Cryptographic Management selects and enforces the approved transmission encryption standards.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 5 Protect Systems from Malicious Software
rationale: Req 5 requires anti-malware solutions on all in-scope systems that are kept current, perform periodic scans and cannot be disabled by users. Endpoint Security hardens endpoints and deploys anti-malware and EDR under those conditions.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.2 Bespoke and Custom Software Security
rationale: Req 6.2 requires bespoke and custom software to be developed securely, with developer training, code review before release and prevention of common coding vulnerabilities. Secure Development integrates security assurance into design, coding, build and release.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.2.1 Secure Development Processes
rationale: Req 6.2.1 requires a documented software development process based on industry standards that incorporates security throughout the lifecycle. The Software Development Lifecycle control provides that documented process.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.3 Security Vulnerabilities Identified and Addressed
rationale: Req 6.3 requires identification of security vulnerabilities through industry sources, risk ranking, and patching within defined timeframes. Vulnerability Testing identifies and drives mitigation of exploitable weaknesses.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.3.2 Inventory of Bespoke and Custom Software
rationale: Req 6.3.2 requires an inventory of bespoke and custom software and third-party components to support vulnerability management. System Asset Management maintains the application and component inventory that scanning and patching depend on.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.4.3 Payment Page Script Management and Req 11.6.1 Change and Tamper Detection
rationale: Req 6.4.3 requires payment page scripts to be authorized, integrity-assured and inventoried, and 11.6.1 requires a change-and-tamper detection mechanism for payment pages evaluated at least weekly. Continuous Monitoring provides the automated detection of unauthorized changes to those pages.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 6.5 Change Control for System Components
rationale: Req 6.5 requires changes to system components to follow a documented change control process with impact assessment, approval, testing and rollback. Change Management ensures changes are risk-assessed, approved and auditable.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 7 Restrict Access by Business Need to Know
rationale: Req 7 requires access to system components and cardholder data to be limited to the least privileges needed, assigned by job function and reviewed at least every six months. Identity Management enforces least privilege, separation of duties and periodic access review.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 8 Identify Users and Authenticate Access
rationale: Req 8 requires unique user IDs, lifecycle management of accounts (8.2.4 to 8.2.6), strong authentication factors (8.3.6 password length and complexity) and multi-factor authentication for all access into the CDE (8.4.2). Identity Management governs identity issuance, authentication strength and account lifecycle for human and machine identities.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 9 Restrict Physical Access to Cardholder Data
rationale: Req 9 requires physical access controls to facilities and systems holding cardholder data, visitor management and media controls. Access Controls prevents unauthorized physical access to facilities, secure areas and media.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 9.4 Media with Cardholder Data Secured and Destroyed
rationale: Req 9.4 requires media containing cardholder data to be classified, securely stored, transported and destroyed when no longer needed. Classification & Handling applies the sensitivity-based handling and destruction protocols to that media.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 10 Log and Monitor All Access
rationale: Req 10 requires audit logs for all access to system components and cardholder data, protection of log integrity, daily review of logs and alerting on critical events. Continuous Monitoring provides the automated log collection, review and alerting that Req 10 requires.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 10.7 Failures of Critical Security Control Systems
rationale: Req 10.7 requires failures of critical security control systems to be detected, alerted and responded to promptly. Security Thresholds defines the alarm criteria and decision rules that trigger that response.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 11.3 Vulnerability Scanning
rationale: Req 11.3 requires internal and external vulnerability scans at least quarterly and after significant change, with external scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor. Vulnerability Testing performs and tracks remediation of those scans.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 11.4 Penetration Testing
rationale: Req 11.4 requires external and internal penetration testing at least annually and after significant change, including segmentation testing. Penetration Testing simulates adversarial attacks to evaluate system resilience.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 11.5 Intrusion Detection and Change Detection
rationale: Req 11.5.1 requires intrusion detection or prevention techniques to detect and alert on intrusions, and 11.5.2 requires a change-detection mechanism such as file integrity monitoring. IOC Detection identifies indicators of compromise across enterprise systems.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.4 PCI DSS Compliance Program and Req 12.11 Verification of Operations
rationale: Req 12.4 requires executive management to establish responsibility for the PCI DSS compliance program, and 12.11 requires service providers to review personnel compliance with security policies quarterly. Performing Security Assessments assesses control effectiveness through systematic testing.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.4 PCI DSS Compliance Program
rationale: Req 12.4.1 requires executive responsibility for protection of cardholder data and a PCI DSS compliance program, and Appendix A3 requires designated entities to validate compliance continuously. Cybersecurity Regulatory Compliance aligns security controls with contractual obligations such as PCI DSS and maintains continuous compliance.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.6 Security Awareness Education
rationale: Req 12.6 requires a formal security awareness program for all personnel on hire and at least annually, including phishing and social engineering and acceptable use. Cybersecurity Training delivers that foundational and role-based awareness.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.7 Personnel Screening
rationale: Req 12.7 requires potential personnel with access to the cardholder data environment to be screened before hire. Human Resources ensures personnel practices, including screening, uphold confidentiality and integrity.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.8 Third-Party Service Providers
rationale: Req 12.8 requires a list of TPSPs, written agreements acknowledging their responsibilities, due diligence before engagement and at least annual monitoring of their PCI DSS compliance status. Third-Party Risk Management performs the due diligence, contracting and monitoring of service providers.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.10 Incident Response Plan
rationale: Req 12.10 requires an incident response plan that is tested annually, includes 24/7 personnel availability, and covers roles, communication, containment and business recovery. Incident Response: Cybersecurity coordinates the technical response across infrastructure and applications.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.10.3 Personnel Available 24/7
rationale: Req 12.10.3 requires specific personnel to be designated and available at all times to respond to suspected or confirmed incidents. The Incident Response Team maintains synchronized internal coordination during active incidents.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.10.1 Notification of Payment Brands and Acquirers
rationale: Req 12.10.1 requires the incident response plan to include procedures for notifying payment brands and acquirers. Regulatory Reporting meets external breach-reporting obligations in time and content.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.10.2 Annual Incident Response Plan Testing
rationale: Req 12.10.2 requires the incident response plan to be reviewed and tested at least annually, including all elements listed in 12.10.1. Tabletop Exercises (BCDR) test incident response and recovery readiness through structured simulations.

PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement: Req 12.10.5 Monitoring Alerts Included in Incident Response
rationale: Req 12.10.5 requires the incident response plan to include response to alerts from intrusion detection, anti-malware, file integrity monitoring and change-detection systems. Incident Management ensures rapid identification, containment and recovery from those detected events.
